 Luka Dončić finished Sunday’s win over the Suns with 43 points (13-of-28 FGs, 12-of-14 FTs), three rebounds, nine assists and five three-pointers. 
 With no Austin Reaves (heel), Dončić was even more assertive on offense at the start of Sunday’s game. The Lakers star scored 20 points in the first quarter, shooting 7-of-8 from the foul line. Dončić did a lot of his damage against the Suns’ starters, scoring 32 points in the first and third quarters. He finished one assist shy of a double-double, continuing to play like a bona fide MVP candidate. The Lakers play three games next week, starting with the Hornets on Tuesday.

 Luka Dončić (ankle) finished Wednesday’s win over the Bucks with 32 points (10-of-25 FGs, 7-of-10 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, three steals and five three-pointers. 
 Dončić has scored at least 30 points in each of his last nine appearances. However, there was a concerning moment when the Lakers star appeared to tweak his ankle during the fourth quarter. The benches were being cleared at this point, so Dončić returned to the Lakers’ locker room with a team trainer with 4:23 remaining in the fourth quarter. We’ll see if he lands on the injury report for Friday’s game against the Spurs, especially with Austin Reaves (heel) leaving Wednesday’s victory during the third quarter.

 Luka Dončić accumulated 32 points (11-of-22 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), eight rebounds, 10 assists, five steals and two blocks over 39 minutes to lead the Lakers to a 124-114 win over the Hawks on Monday. 
 Dončić fell short of the 40-point plateau in his return from a one-game absence due to a minor back issue, but showed no signs of rust, turning in another spectacular all-around performance that left him two rebounds shy of a triple-double. He scored 18 of his 32 points after halftime, helping Los Angeles withstand a late Atlanta rally before pulling away in the closing minutes. The Lakers were also without Austin Reaves (illness) in this one, making Dončić’s latest all-around performance even more impressive. The 27-year-old franchise cornerstone has been virtually unstoppable through the early stages of the season and has quickly established himself as the frontrunner in the MVP race.

 Luka Dončić (back) is off the injury report for Monday’s matchup with the Hawks. 
 Luka sat out Sunday with a back issue, although it may have just been precautionary since the Lakers play a Sunday-Monday back-to-back set. Austin Reaves scored a season-high 43 points in Sunday’s victory over the Pistons, but he’s now listed as questionable with an illness. Even if Reaves is available, he’s likely going to take a backseat to Dončić in the scoring department, as he’s done all season.

Austin Reaves took on primary playmaking in that game and struggled, shooting 6-of-16 from the field and committing eight turnovers. As for the starting lineup, Quentin Grimes could replace Dončić.

 Luka Dončić went off in Friday’s win over the Trail Blazers, finishing with 53 points (17-of-33 FGs, 14-of-18 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, one steal and five three-pointers. 
 Dončić finished Friday’s victory with his 11th 50-point game, moving past Kareem Abdul-Jabbar and Allen Iverson to land in tenth on the league’s all-time list. But that wasn’t the only history the Lakers star made on Friday. Dončić has tallied at least 35 points, five rebounds, and five assists in seven straight games, tying Oscar Robertson for the longest such streak in league history. Also, Dončić, who outscored Portland 20-15 in the third quarter, has scored at least 40 points in four straight games. He’s on an incredible run, which is great for those rostering Dončić.

 Luka Dončić had himself a night with 40 points (11-of-23 FGs, 12-of-13 FTs), nine rebounds, seven assists, a steal, a block, six 3-pointers, and six turnovers in 116-103 win over the Kings. 
 Luka’s MVP campaign continues in Sacramento where he puts another massive statement game against the Kings. He took over in the third quarter, and the Lakers separated themselves against the Kings in this game. He’s been everything you could’ve wanted and more this season and the hope is that he doesn’t get hurt.

 Luka Dončić led the Lakers with 42 points (14-of-24 FGs, 8-of-10 FTs), seven rebounds, 13 assists, two steals and six three-pointers in a 138-117 win over the Heat on Monday. 
 It has been an unreal start to the season for Dončić, and Monday’s performance was just another chapter. He has scored at least 35 points and knocked down at least six three-pointers in each of his last five appearances, while going for at least 40 in four of those outings. The one game he didn’t score 40, he had 37, which was also the only game during this stretch where he shot below 50 percent from the floor. Dončić set a new season high for assists in this game as well. He has been an elite offensive engine, and he’ll look to stay hot against the Kings on Wednesday.

 Luka Dončić finished Sunday’s win over the Raptors with 45 points (12-of-23 FGs, 13-of-13 FTs), 15 rebounds, six assists, five steals, one block and eight three-pointers. 
 Dončić put on a show Sunday night, shooting high percentages from the field and the foul line as part of an elite stat line. With the Lakers’ deep reserves failing to put the Raptors away, head coach JJ Redick had to insert four starters back into the game. That got Dončić four more points from the foul line. The lone negative was the seven turnovers, but the stat line was so robust that few will complain. The Lakers play four games next week, starting with the Heat on Monday.

 Kevon Looney finished Tuesday’s loss to the Hornets with four points (2-of-3 FGs) and seven rebounds.
 With Walker Kessler (leg) out, the Lakers turned to Looney to start at center on Tuesday. While the veteran center grabbed seven rebounds, he played only 17 minutes, and his mobility was an issue. With Sandro Mamukelashvili (3/3/2/1) shooting 1-of-8 from the field, Lakers head coach JJ Redick eventually turned to two-way contract player Carson Cooper. While his numbers (3/4/2 in 18 minutes) won’t jump off the page, Cooper’s contributions as a rebounder and defender were one reason why the Lakers were able to rally. Kessler is expected to be available for Wednesday’s game against the Jazz, so Looney may find himself out of the rotation once again.

 Quentin Grimes amassed 47 points (16-of-24 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, three assists, one steal and 10 three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Hornets.
 Grimes had the best game of his career on Tuesday, and the Lakers needed it, trailing by as much as 18 late in the third quarter before rallying to win in overtime. Grimes scored 21 points in the fourth quarter alone, outscoring the Hornets by four, and his three-pointer with 1.7 seconds left forced overtime. Austin Reaves (heel) is supposed to test his injured heel on Wednesday before that night’s game against the Jazz, so more should be learned about how much time he’ll miss. Grimes will start as long as Reaves is out, and he’s worth rostering until that changes. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Darius Garland accumulated 20 points (5-of-15 FGs, 8-of-8 FTs), three rebounds, seven assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Jazz.
 While Garland kept the turnovers in check, committing one, and recorded a full stat line, he had a tough night shooting the basketball. The Clippers guard was 5-of-15 from the field, a far cry from his 50.6 percent shooting for the season. The biggest concern for him in fantasy basketball has been the turnovers, so there’s no need to lose sleep over Garland having an off shooting night.

This was Hachimura’s second game this season with at least 20 points, five rebounds and five assists. Even better for fantasy managers was his 70 percent shooting from the field, a strong output for a player shooting 41.5 percent on the season.
